stage1_callout: Nothing clears the gate. Of 8,160 configurations with at least 200 trades, zero reach profit factor 1.20 at realistic cost. Only 6 of them exceed 1.00 at all, the best at 1.045. The median configuration sits at 0.556. Strip the fees entirely and the median is still 0.960 — below breakeven.
lit_callout: The filter does not survive contact with new data. 75 configurations clear PF 1.20 in sample. Out of sample 4 of them still do — 5%. The median out-of-sample profit factor of that hand-picked group is 0.945, below breakeven. The single best in-sample config (1.907) scored 0.671 out of sample. And the survivors trade about 0.11 times a day — roughly one trade a fortnight, which fails the current phase constraint on its own.
prop_note: 36% of accounts pass with the best configuration at real cost, and 64% breach the 8% max loss. Buying challenges at roughly €30 each to run a negative-expectancy engine is a losing trade on its own: the accounts that do pass are then funded with a system whose edge is below zero. The daily-loss cap is never the thing that kills it — at 1% risk and about one trade a day, the account bleeds down to the overall cap instead.
survival_callout: Only GBPUSD carried anything into the unseen year, and it turned out to be one cell rather than an effect. 9 configurations cleared PF 1.20 on the fit window and 5 of them cleared it again on the test year. Against a base rate of 0.4% that looks overwhelming — until you look at what those configurations are. All nine are the same setup: a 1-hour range, faded, entered on a close beyond the edge, almost all of them at the 20:00 anchor. They are one observation wearing nine hats, so the significance test does not apply. Gold cleared the gate 2 times in sample and 0 times out of it, with a median of 0.976.
assets_callout: The answer does not change by market. Over one common three-year window, 13 configurations out of 32,640 clear PF 1.20 at realistic cost across all four instruments. The best single result anywhere is 1.439 on GBPUSD. With fees stripped to zero the medians are Gold 0.982, EURUSD 0.948, GBPUSD 0.971, Bitcoin 0.984 — at or below breakeven before a single cost is charged.
anchor_callout:
The method finds session structure exactly where session structure exists — and it is still not enough. Gold, EURUSD and GBPUSD all agree on the same best anchor by median profit factor, the 13:00 NY open, and on the same worst one, the 20:00 NY close. The spread between best and worst anchor is 57% on EURUSD and 56% on GBPUSD, against only 16% on Bitcoin — which is what a market with no opening auction should look like. That is a good sign about the test: it finds session structure where session structure exists and almost none where it does not. But the best anchor on the best instrument still has a median profit factor of 0.789. The session effect is real, measurable, and far too small to trade.

It also disposes of the GBPUSD result above. Its 20:00 anchor is not a session open at all; it is the New York close, and it is the worst anchor on every FX pair by median. That configuration is the luckiest cell of the weakest family.
